content: Gemfibrozil is a medication that is prescribed to help lower cholesterol and certain types of fats in the blood. It is used in combination with dietary changes, such as reducing the intake of cholesterol and fats, to achieve this goal. The accumulation of cholesterol and fats along the walls of arteries, a condition known as atherosclerosis, can restrict blood flow and reduce oxygen supply to the heart, brain, and other parts of the body. By lowering cholesterol and fat levels in the blood, gemfibrozil may help prevent conditions such as heart disease, angina (chest pain), strokes, and heart attacks. In some cases, gemfibrozil may be prescribed for other purposes, so it is important to consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Gemfibrozil is available in tablet and capsule forms and is taken orally. It is typically taken twice daily, 30 minutes before the morning and evening meals. It is essential to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully and to ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take gemfibrozil exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Even if you feel well, continue taking the medication as directed. Do not stop taking gemfibrozil without consulting your doctor. Before starting gemfibrozil, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to gemfibrozil or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially anticoagulants (such as warfarin) and vitamins. If you are using insulin or oral diabetes medications, your dosage may need adjustment, as gemfibrozil can increase blood sugar levels. Discuss any changes with your doctor. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have a history of ulcers, diabetes, or gallbladder, kidney, or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking gemfibrozil, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking gemfibrozil. While taking gemfibrozil, it is important to follow a low-cholesterol, low-fat diet. This diet should include foods such as cottage cheese, fat-free milk, fish (not canned in oil), vegetables, poultry, egg whites, and polyunsaturated oils and margarines (such as corn, safflower, canola, and soybean oils). Avoid foods high in fat, such as fatty meats, liver, egg yolks, whole milk, cream, butter, shortening, lard, pastries, cakes, cookies, gravy, peanut butter, chocolate, olives, potato chips, coconut, cheese (other than cottage cheese), coconut oil, palm oil, and fried foods. If you miss a dose of gemfibrozil, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Gemfibrozil may cause side effects. Minor side effects include stomach pain, diarrhea, constipation, vomiting, gas, headache, dizziness, blurred vision, and flushing. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Severe side effects, such as muscle pain or weakness, require immediate medical attention. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store gemfibrozil in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of outdated or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. It is important to keep all appointments with your doctor and the laboratory, as your doctor will order tests to monitor your response to gemfibrozil. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have any questions about refilling your prescription. Gemfibrozil is also sold under the brand name Lopid®.
